mainTopic: Laws of the end of קריאת שמע: repeating 'אמת', the night-time ציצית paragraph, the order of the paragraphs, and reading שמע with תפילין
overview: The amud opens with the word 'אמת' that is joined to the end of שמע, and asks whether it is said again to begin the next ברכה. רבי יוחנן says yes and רבה says no. Then the גמרא discusses the ציצית paragraph at night: ארץ ישראל said a shortened version, and אביי concludes that we begin it and say all of it. חייא בר רב adds that 'אמת' is needed only if 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' was said, and a short 'מודים אנחנו לך' text covers the mention of יציאת מצרים. Next the גמרא gives two reasons why the שמע paragraph comes first: עול מלכות שמים before עול מצוות, and the count of learning, teaching, and doing. A story about רב saying שמע before putting on תפילין is challenged from a ברייתא about a grave-digger. In the end it is explained by his late messenger. עולא and רבי יוחנן then teach how lacking it is to read שמע without תפילין. The amud ends as רבי יוחנן begins a teaching about accepting עול מלכות שמים completely, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse that links God's Name to 'Truth'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק 'וה׳ אלהים אמת', which joins God's Name directly to the word 'אמת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the Lord, God, is True."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from ירמיהו that puts 'ה׳ אלהים' right next to 'אמת'. This is the source for attaching 'אמת' to the end of שמע, and it sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק joins God's Name and 'אמת', we say 'ה׳ אלהיכם אמת' together without stopping. That raises a practical question: once 'אמת' has been said as part of that phrase, does the ברכה that begins with 'אמת' need it said again?

keyTerms.meaning: Truth; also the first word of the ברכה after שמע (אמת ויציב)

phrases.english: "And the Lord, God, is True."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 10:10

steps.triggerLanguage: וַה׳ אֱלֹהִים אֱמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion (from before this section) about joining 'אמת' to the end of שמע, and serves as the base for the coming question.
steps.raayaObject: That 'אמת' belongs right after 'ה׳ אלהיכם' with no break.

steps.title: Do we say 'אמת' a second time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether one repeats 'אמת' when beginning the ברכה of אמת ויציב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he go back and say 'אמת' again, or does he not go back and say 'אמת' again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question. After saying 'ה׳ אלהיכם אמת', does a person say 'אמת' again to open the next ברכה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one word 'אמת' has two jobs: it finishes the phrase from the פסוק, and it opens the ברכה of אמת ויציב. The question is whether a single 'אמת' covers both jobs or whether each needs its own.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether to say 'אמת' at all. Everyone agrees it is said once. The question is only whether it is said a second time.

phrases.english: Does he go back and say "Emet" again,
or does he not go back and say "Emet" again?

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹזֵר וְאוֹמֵר ״אֱמֶת״, אוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וְאוֹמֵר ״אֱמֶת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the joining of 'אמת' to God's Name and asks what follows from it in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'אמת' is repeated at the start of the ברכה of אמת ויציב after it was already said attached to 'ה׳ אלהיכם'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Say it again
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that one does repeat 'אמת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: He goes back and says 'אמת' again.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer comes from רבי יוחנן, quoted by רבי אבהו: yes, say 'אמת' a second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, the first 'אמת' belongs to the end of שמע and the ברכה of אמת ויציב needs its own opening word. So the word is said twice.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who passes on רבי יוחנן's teaching
A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
He goes back and says "Emet" again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question.

steps.title: רבה: Do not say it again
steps.stepSummary: רבה disagrees and holds that 'אמת' is not repeated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: He does not go back and say 'אמת' again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the opposite answer: say 'אמת' only once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, the single 'אמת' attached to 'ה׳ אלהיכם' also serves as the opening of the ברכה. Saying it twice would be unnecessary.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת. רבי יוחנן says to repeat 'אמת' and רבה says to say it only once.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
He does not go back and say "Emet" again.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן's answer.

steps.title: רבה teases a חזן who said 'אמת' twice
steps.stepSummary: A חזן before רבה said 'אמת אמת' twice, and רבה joked that the love of truth had gripped him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man went down to lead the prayers before רבה. רבה heard him say 'אמת, אמת' two times. רבה said: All this 'אמת, אמת' has grabbed hold of this fellow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing רבה acting on his own opinion. When a חזן repeated 'אמת', רבה made fun of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that רבה's view was not just theory. He considered the double 'אמת' out of place enough to joke about it in public. The story backs up רבה's position from step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down before him, meaning he led the prayers

phrases.english: A certain man went down to lead the prayer before Rabba.
phrases.notes: 'Went down' is how the גמרא describes leading the תפילה, since the חזן's spot was lower.

phrases.english: Rabba heard him say
"Emet," "Emet," two times.
Rabba said:
All this "Emet, Emet" has grabbed hold of this one!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דִּנְחֵית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבה's view from step 4 in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה objected to saying 'אמת' twice, matching his ruling.

steps.title: רב יוסף praises a report about the night-time שמע in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף praises a teaching brought by רב שמואל בר יהודה: at ערבית in ארץ ישראל they said a shortened ציצית paragraph that ended with 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם אמת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: How excellent is this teaching! When רב שמואל בר יהודה came, he said: In ארץ ישראל, at ערבית, they say: 'Speak to the children of Israel and say to them... I am the Lord your God, True.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף introduces a report about how people in ארץ ישראל said שמע at night. They recited only the opening and closing words of the ציצית paragraph, ending with 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם אמת'. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the paragraph was cut short, they still kept its first line and its ending, and 'אמת' was still joined to 'ה׳ אלהיכם'. רב יוסף calls this teaching excellent, and the גמרא will go on to discuss it.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that in ארץ ישראל, the joining of 'ה׳ אלהיכם' to 'אמת' was kept even in a shortened night-time version of the ציצית paragraph.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
How excellent is this teaching,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה אֲמַר:
phrases.english: for when Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda came, he said:
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל and brought their practice with him.

phrases.english: In the West, at the evening prayer, they say:
"Speak to the children of Israel and say to them,
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:38. This is the start of the ציצית paragraph. They then skip to its last words.

phrases.english: I am the Lord your God, True."
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:41, with 'אמת' attached at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כַּמָּה מְעַלְּיָא הָא שְׁמַעְתְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the question of repeating 'אמת' to a related report about the night-time form of the ציצית paragraph, still ending with 'ה׳ אלהיכם אמת'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל at ערבית, they said a shortened ציצית paragraph made of its opening and its closing words, ending with 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם אמת'.

steps.title: אביי questions what is so praiseworthy about the custom
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the custom praised by רב יוסף. רב rules that one who begins the ציצית paragraph at night must finish it, yet the ארץ ישראל custom began it and stopped partway.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What is so great about this? Didn't רב כהנא say in the name of רב: One should not begin the ציצית paragraph at night, but if he began, he must finish it?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's praise of the ארץ ישראל custom. He shows that it seems to go against a ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The custom from step 6 was to say the start of the ציצית paragraph and then jump to the end. רב's rule is that you may skip the paragraph at night, but once you start it you must say all of it. A shortened version looks like starting without finishing.

keyTerms.meaning: but if he began, he finishes

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב יוסף, who praised the custom in the previous step.

phrases.english: What is so excellent about it?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Kahana say that Rav said:
One should not begin,
phrases.notes: He means the ציצית paragraph at night.

phrases.english: and if he began, he finishes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מַאי מְעַלְּיוּתָא? וְהָא אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the custom praised in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ארץ ישראל custom of saying a shortened ציצית paragraph at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב rules that one who begins must finish. The custom begins the paragraph and does not finish it.

steps.title: Blocking the defense that 'And say to them' is not a real beginning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers defending the custom by saying its opening words do not count as starting the paragraph. It then rejects that defense, because רב himself said 'ואמרת אליהם' does count as a beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that 'And say to them' is not counted as beginning the paragraph, didn't רב שמואל בר יצחק say in the name of רב: 'Speak to the children of Israel' is not a beginning, but 'and say to them' is a beginning?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes off an easy escape before anyone can use it. You cannot claim the custom never really started the paragraph.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shortened version included 'דבר אל בני ישראל ואמרת אליהם'. One might argue those words are just an introduction and not the start of the ציצית paragraph. But רב said that while 'דבר אל בני ישראל' is not a beginning, 'ואמרת אליהם' is, so the custom did begin the paragraph.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say (introduces a possible defense)
'Speak to the children of Israel', a common Torah opening

steps.confusionAlert: This is still אביי's challenge, not a new answer. The 'if you say' line is a defense he raises only to knock it down.

phrases.english: And if you say that "And say to them"
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:38

phrases.english: is not considered a beginning —

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: but didn't Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak say that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: ״דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״ לָא הָוֵי הַתְחָלָה,
phrases.english: "Speak to the children of Israel" is not a beginning,
"and say to them" is a beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא ״וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵיהֶם״ לָא הָוֵי הַתְחָלָה — וְהָאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 7 by rejecting a possible defense.
steps.kashyaTarget: The defense that the custom never truly began the paragraph.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב defines 'ואמרת אליהם' as the beginning, and the custom said those words.

steps.title: רב פפא: in ארץ ישראל, the beginning is only 'And make for them ציצית'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא defends the custom. The people of ארץ ישראל hold that even 'ואמרת אליהם' is not a beginning, so they never actually started the paragraph.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: In the West they hold that even 'and say to them' is not a beginning, until one says 'and make for them ציצית'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers אביי's challenge. ארץ ישראל simply defines the beginning of the paragraph differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב counted 'ואמרת אליהם' as the start, but ארץ ישראל did not follow that view. For them, the real content starts only at 'ועשו להם ציצית'. Since the shortened version skipped those words, by their view they never began, so there was nothing to finish.

keyTerms.meaning: they hold, it is their view
in the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
'and they shall make for themselves ציצית'

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
In the West they hold
phrases.notes: "The West" is how Babylonian sages refer to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: that "and say to them" is also not a beginning
until he says "and make for them ציצית."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: קָסָבְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 7 and 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the point at which the paragraph counts as begun.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The custom began the paragraph by saying 'ואמרת אליהם' and failed to finish it.
steps.terutzMaskana: In ארץ ישראל, the beginning is only 'ועשו להם ציצית', so the custom never began the paragraph.

steps.title: אביי: we begin like ארץ ישראל and finish like רב
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes the practice for his community. They begin the ציצית paragraph at night because ארץ ישראל does so, and once they begin they say all of it, following רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Therefore, we do begin, since they begin in the West. And once we begin, we also finish, because רב כהנא said in the name of רב: One should not begin, but if he began, he finishes.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the practical bottom line that comes out of the discussion. It combines the ארץ ישראל custom with רב's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From ארץ ישראל, אביי learns that saying the paragraph at night is proper, so his community starts it. Since his community counts 'ואמרת אליהם' as a beginning, רב's rule then requires them to say the whole paragraph.
steps.whatToRemember: We say the ציצית paragraph at night like ארץ ישראל, and we say all of it because of רב's rule that once you begin, you finish.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the full ציצית paragraph is said at ערבית.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Therefore,
we do begin,
since they begin in the West,
and since we have begun,
we finish as well.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב
phrases.english: For Rav Kahana said that Rav said:
one should not begin, but if he began, he finishes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הִלְכָּךְ, אֲנַן אַתְחוֹלֵי מַתְחֲלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical conclusion from רב פפא's answer together with רב's rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: At ערבית we begin the ציצית paragraph and say the whole thing.

steps.title: חייא בר רב: saying 'אמת' depends on saying 'I am ה׳ your God'
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב rules that at night, one who said 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' must continue with 'אמת'. One who did not say it does not need to.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב said: If one said 'I am ה׳ your God', he must say 'אמת'. If he did not say 'I am ה׳ your God', he does not need to say 'אמת'.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement links the end of the ציצית paragraph to the word 'אמת' that follows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'אמת' right after 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' completes the connection between them. If the ציצית paragraph was not said at all, that connection is not needed, so 'אמת' is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I am ה׳ your God', the end of the ציצית paragraph

phrases.english: Chiyya bar Rav said:
If he said "I am ה׳ your God,"
he must say "Truth."
phrases.notes: At night, this "אמת" is the opening word of the next ברכה, אמת ואמונה.

phrases.english: If he did not say "I am ה׳ your God,"
he does not need to say "Truth."

steps.triggerLanguage: חִיָּיא בַּר רַב אָמַר: אָמַר ״אֲנִי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם״, צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר ״אֱמֶת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the link between 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' and 'אמת' from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אמת' is required only if 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' was said.

steps.title: But he still must mention the Exodus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges חייא בר רב. If someone did not say 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' at night and so does not continue with 'אמת', he never mentions יציאת מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he still needs to mention the Exodus from Egypt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on חייא בר רב's ruling. A person who skipped the ending at night seems to miss the מצוה of mentioning יציאת מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חייא בר רב said that at night, someone who did not say 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' does not need to say 'אמת'. But mentioning יציאת מצרים is required at night too. The ending of the ציצית paragraph and the 'אמת' blessing are where that mention happens, so skipping them seems to leave the obligation unfulfilled.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely, a word that opens a challenge
He needs to, he is required to

phrases.english: But surely he needs to mention
phrases.notes: "He" is the person from step 11, who did not say 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' at night.

phrases.english: the Exodus from Egypt!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בָּעֵי לְאַדְכּוֹרֵי יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of חייא בר רב in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: חייא בר רב's ruling that one who did not say 'אני ה׳ אלהיכם' at night need not say 'אמת'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a duty to mention יציאת מצרים at night. Skipping both the paragraph's ending and 'אמת' seems to skip that duty.

steps.title: He says a short thanksgiving text instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the person says a short replacement text, 'מודים אנחנו לך', which mentions the Exodus and the miracles at the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says this: 'We thank You, ה׳ our God, Who took us out of the land of Egypt, redeemed us from the house of slavery, did miracles and mighty acts for us at the sea, and we sang to You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The person does mention יציאת מצרים, but he uses a short replacement text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that the only way to mention the Exodus is the end of the ציצית paragraph or 'אמת'. The answer shows another way: a short prayer of thanks that names the Exodus, the redemption, and the miracles at the sea. So חייא בר רב's ruling stands, and the person still fulfills his duty.

keyTerms.meaning: We give thanks to You, the opening of the replacement text
And we sang to You, referring to the song at the sea

phrases.english: He says it this way:
"We give thanks to You, Lord our God,
Who took us out of the land of Egypt
and redeemed us from the house of slavery

phrases.aramaic: וְעָשִׂיתָ לָנוּ נִסִּים וּגְבוּרוֹת עַל הַיָּם
phrases.english: and did for us miracles and mighty acts at the sea
and we sang to You."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies how the obligation is fulfilled: through a short alternate text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Skipping the ending means the Exodus is never mentioned at night
steps.terutzMaskana: He mentions the Exodus through the short 'מודים אנחנו לך' text, so חייא בר רב's ruling stands
steps.whatToRemember: At night, someone who skipped the end of the ציצית paragraph can still fulfill the mention of יציאת מצרים with the short 'מודים אנחנו לך' text.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: why שמע comes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, where רבי יהושע בן קרחה asks why the שמע paragraph comes before והיה אם שמוע.
steps.simpleTranslation: [We learned in the משנה:] רבי יהושע בן קרחה said: Why does the paragraph of שמע come first? And so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the משנה. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה asked why the paragraphs of קריאת שמע are in this order. Its answer was that a person first accepts the kingship of Heaven and only then accepts the מצוות. The גמרא quotes the start of that question so it can bring a different reason in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא in the משנה who asks why שמע comes first
And so on, meaning the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said:
Why does the paragraph of "Shema" come first, and so on.
phrases.notes: The "and so on" stands for the rest of the משנה: first accept Heaven's kingship, then the מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה לָמָּה קָדְמָה פָּרָשַׁת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the night-time ציצית discussion and returns to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה explains the order of the paragraphs of קריאת שמע: kingship of Heaven before מצוות.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי: learning, then teaching, then doing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי שמעון בן יוחי's reason for the order of the paragraphs. שמע is about learning and comes before והיה אם שמוע, which is about teaching. והיה אם שמוע comes before ויאמר, which is about doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says, it makes sense that שמע comes before והיה אם שמוע, because this one is to learn and that one is to teach. And והיה אם שמוע comes before ויאמר, because this one is to learn and that one is to do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a second reason for the order of the paragraphs. Each paragraph is placed according to the order of learning, teaching, and doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה explained the order by the kind of acceptance: first Heaven's kingship, then מצוות‎. רבי שמעון בן יוחי explains it by a natural order of steps. First you learn (שמע), then you teach others (והיה אם שמוע), and the paragraph about doing a מצוה‎ (ויאמר, ציצית) comes last.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
The תנא who gives the learning-teaching-doing reason
It is logical, it makes sense

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
It makes sense that "Shema" should come before
"VeHaya im Shamoa" —
for this one is to learn, and that one is to teach.
And "VeHaya im Shamoa" comes before "VaYomer" —
phrases.notes: ויאמר is the third paragraph, the ציצית paragraph, which opens with the word ויאמר.

phrases.english: for this one is to learn, and that one is to do.
phrases.notes: "This one" is והיה אם שמוע and "that one" is the ציצית paragraph. The next step reads והיה אם שמוע as the teaching paragraph.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר בַּדִּין הוּא שֶׁיַּקְדִּים שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reason for the order the משנה asked about
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The paragraphs follow the order of learning (שמע), then teaching (והיה אם שמוע), then doing (ויאמר).
steps.confusionAlert: In the second comparison, 'this one' now means והיה אם שמוע, not שמע. Each comparison sets the earlier paragraph against the one after it. The next step makes clear that the גמרא reads this as והיה אם שמוע being the 'teaching' paragraph.
steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons for the order of קריאת שמע: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says Heaven's kingship comes before מצוות, and רבי שמעון בן יוחי says learning comes before teaching, which comes before doing.

steps.title: The paragraphs contain more than רבי שמעון בן יוחי said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בן יוחי's reason. The שמע paragraph also commands teaching and doing, and והיה אם שמוע also commands doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you mean that שמע only has learning, and no teaching or doing? But it says 'teach them,' 'bind them,' and 'write them'! And does והיה אם שמוע only have teaching, and no doing? But it says 'bind them' and 'write them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason from the last step. Each paragraph seems to contain more types of מצוות than רבי שמעון בן יוחי gave it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחי linked each paragraph to one activity: learning, teaching, or doing. But the פסוקים in שמע include teaching (ושננתם) and doing (תפילין and מזוזה). The פסוקים in והיה אם שמוע also include doing. So the neat one-paragraph, one-activity picture seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (opens a surprised challenge)

phrases.english: Is that to say that "Shema" contains learning,
but does not contain teaching and doing?!
But it is written: "And you shall teach them,"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:7

phrases.english: "And you shall bind them," "And you shall write them"!
phrases.notes: דברים 6:8–9. These are מצוות you do: תפילין and מזוזה.

phrases.english: And furthermore: "VeHaya im Shamoa"
is it only teaching that it contains,
and it does not contain doing?
But it is written: "And you shall bind them," "And you shall write them"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ ״שְׁמַע״ — לִלְמוֹד אִית בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in the ברייתא in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's claim that שמע is for learning and והיה אם שמוע is for teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים themselves show that both paragraphs include more activities than he gave them.

steps.title: Ordering by how many kinds of מצוות each paragraph has
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי meant that שמע has all three (learning, teaching, doing), והיה אם שמוע has two, and ויאמר has only one. The paragraph with more comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he means this: it is right that שמע comes before והיה אם שמוע, because שמע has learning, teaching, and doing. והיה אם שמוע comes before ויאמר, because it has teaching and doing, while ויאמר has only doing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads רבי שמעון בן יוחי's words. He was not giving each paragraph only one activity. He was counting how many activities each one contains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reading accepts the challenge: שמע really does contain learning, teaching, and doing. The order goes from the fullest paragraph to the least full: three activities, then two, then one. So the order still holds, and the facts from the פסוקים are respected.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what he means (a rereading of an earlier statement)
It is right / it makes sense that
The third paragraph of שמע, about ציצית

steps.whatToRemember: The order of the שמע paragraphs follows how many kinds of מצוות each one holds: שמע has three (learning, teaching, doing), והיה אם שמוע has two, and ויאמר has one.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he means:
It is right that "Shema" should come first
before "VeHaya im Shamoa,"
because this one is for learning, teaching, and doing.
"VeHaya im Shamoa" comes before "VaYomer,"
because this one has teaching and doing,
while "VaYomer" has only doing alone.
phrases.notes: ויאמר is the ציצית paragraph, and wearing ציצית is a מצוה you do.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought each paragraph was matched to only one activity.
steps.terutzMaskana: The paragraphs are ordered by how many activities each contains: three, then two, then one.

steps.title: Why not use רבי יהושע בן קרחה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון בן יוחי needed a new reason, since the משנה already gave רבי יהושע בן קרחה's reason for שמע coming first.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he could have learned this from רבי יהושע בן קרחה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון בן יוחי gave his own reason. The משנה already explained why שמע comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהושע בן קרחה said שמע comes first so that a person accepts the yoke of Heaven before the yoke of מצוות. If that reason already works, a second reason seems unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him derive it (from somewhere else)

phrases.english: But let him derive it
from the words of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for רבי שמעון בן יוחי's reason, now that it has been clarified.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי שמעון בן יוחי's separate reason
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's reason already explains why שמע comes first, so a new reason seems extra.

steps.title: He gave one reason and added another
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי agrees with רבי יהושע בן קרחה. He is adding a second reason: שמע also contains learning, teaching, and doing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is giving one reason and another. One: so that a person first accepts upon himself the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, and afterward the yoke of מצוות. And another: because שמע contains these other things too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no argument. רבי שמעון בן יוחי accepts the first reason and adds a second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two reasons work together and do not compete. The first reason is accepting Heaven's rule before the מצוות. The second is that שמע holds all three activities: learning, teaching, and doing.

keyTerms.meaning: He says one reason and also another
The yoke of the kingdom of Heaven: accepting הקב״ה as King

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons why שמע comes first: accepting עול מלכות שמים before עול מצוות, and the fact that שמע contains learning, teaching, and doing.

phrases.english: He is saying one reason and another:
One: so that he should accept upon himself
the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven first,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ יְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל מִצְוֹת,
phrases.english: and afterward accept upon himself the yoke of מצוות;
and another: because it contains
these other things.
phrases.notes: He means learning, teaching, and doing, from the reason we just saw.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא וְעוֹד קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by showing that the two reasons fit together.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון בן יוחי seemed to ignore or reject רבי יהושע בן קרחה's reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: He accepts it and adds a second reason.

steps.title: רב's morning order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells that רב washed his hands, said קריאת שמע, put on תפילין, and then prayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב washed his hands, said קריאת שמע, put on תפילין, and prayed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a short story. It describes the order in which רב did his morning מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is the order. רב said שמע before putting on תפילין. This sets up the next step, which questions that order.

phrases.english: Rav washed his hands,
and recited Shema,
and put on tefillin and prayed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מְשִׁי יְדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the order of the morning מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב said שמע before putting on תפילין.

steps.title: A ברייתא puts תפילין before שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's order from a ברייתא about a grave-digger. There, the person washes, puts on תפילין, then says שמע, then prays.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could רב do this? A ברייתא teaches: one who digs a burial niche for a dead person is exempt from קריאת שמע, prayer, תפילין, and all the מצוות of the Torah. When the time for קריאת שמע comes, he goes up, washes his hands, puts on תפילין, says קריאת שמע, and prays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב's behavior using a ברייתא. In the ברייתא, the order of the מצוות is different. The answer comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's order is: washing, תפילין, שמע, תפלה. רב put שמע before תפילין. So the ברייתא seems to show that רב's order was wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But how could he do this?
A burial niche dug into the wall of a burial cave

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not about the grave-digger being פטור. It is about the order at the end of the ברייתא: תפילין before שמע, the opposite of what רב did.

phrases.english: But how could he do this?
But it was taught in a baraita:
One who digs a burial niche for a dead person in the grave
is exempt from reciting Shema and from prayer

phrases.aramaic: וּמִן הַתְּפִילִּין וּמִכׇּל מִצְוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and from tefillin and from all the מצוות stated in the Torah.
When the time for reciting Shema arrives,
he comes up and washes his hands,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין, וְקוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, וּמִתְפַּלֵּל.
phrases.english: and puts on tefillin, recites Shema, and prays.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's order from step 20 with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's practice of saying שמע before putting on תפילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists the order as תפילין, then שמע, which goes against רב's practice.

steps.title: The grave-digger teaching seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: Before dealing with רב, the גמרא points out that the ברייתא itself seems inconsistent: the first part says the digger is פטור, and the last part says he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaching itself is hard to understand! The first part says he is exempt, and the last part says he is obligated?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses from the question on רב to point out a problem inside the ברייתא itself. Its two parts seem to say opposite things about the grave-digger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא says someone digging a grave is פטור from קריאת שמע. The last part describes him coming up, washing, putting on תפילין, and saying שמע, which means he is חייב. Both cannot be true about the same person.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult; the source contradicts itself
The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
phrases.notes: "This" is the grave-digger ברייתא from the step before. The גמרא is setting aside the question on רב for a moment.

phrases.english: the first part says he is exempt,
and the last part says he is obligated?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גוּפָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side question about the ברייתא quoted in step 21, before the גמרא finishes its question on רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the grave-digger ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same ברייתא calls the digger exempt in its first part and obligated in its last part.

steps.title: Two diggers versus one digger
steps.stepSummary: The last part is about two people digging together, and the first part is about one person digging alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not a problem. The last part is about two diggers, and the first part is about one digger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two parts of the ברייתא are about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two people dig, one can stop to say שמע while the other keeps digging, so he is חייב. When one person digs alone, he is busy with the dead and may not stop, so he is פטור. Once each part has its own case, the contradiction is gone.

phrases.english: That is not difficult:
the last part is about two diggers,
and the first part is about one digger.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each part of the ברייתא is about a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both parts seemed to be about the same digger, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first part is about one digger (פטור), and the last part is about two diggers (חייב).

steps.title: Back to the problem with רב's order
steps.stepSummary: Either way, the ברייתא still puts תפילין before שמע, which goes against what רב did.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, this is a problem for רב.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the side question is settled, the גמרא goes back to its main question from step 21. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fixing the contradiction did not change the order in the ברייתא: wash, תפילין, שמע, then pray. רב said שמע first and only then put on תפילין, so the question on רב still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a problem for רב

phrases.english: In any case,
this is a problem for Rav.
phrases.notes: The problem is the order: the ברייתא puts תפילין before שמע, but רב said שמע first.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם קַשְׁיָא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side issue (steps 22-23) and brings back the question of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's order of שמע before תפילין (step 20)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, read either way, has תפילין before שמע.

steps.title: רב follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה
steps.stepSummary: רב holds like רבי יהושע בן קרחה, who said accepting עול מלכות שמים comes first and only then עול מצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב holds like רבי יהושע בן קרחה, who said: first the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, and after that the yoke of the commandments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. It says his order comes from the rule of רבי יהושע בן קרחה in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying שמע is accepting עול מלכות שמים, and putting on תפילין is taking on עול מצות. Since רבי יהושע בן קרחה said עול מלכות שמים comes first, רב said שמע before putting on תפילין. The next step questions whether רבי יהושע בן קרחה's rule really reaches this case.

keyTerms.meaning: The yoke of the kingdom of Heaven; accepting ה׳ as King

phrases.aramaic: רַב כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קָרְחָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rav holds like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha,
who said: the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven comes first,
and after that the yoke of the commandments.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קָרְחָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on רב brought back in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tying רב to a תנא: רב follows a different opinion from the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's order seemed to go against the ברייתא with no support.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה: עול מלכות שמים (שמע) before עול מצות (תפילין).

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן קרחה only spoke about reading before reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: רבי יהושע בן קרחה only taught which paragraph to read first. He never said reading comes before doing a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, רבי יהושע בן קרחה said to put one reading before another reading. But did you hear him say to put reading before doing?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It says רבי יהושע בן קרחה's rule may not cover רב's case at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהושע בן קרחה only compared two paragraphs of קריאת שמע, which are both readings. רב's case compares reading שמע with putting on תפילין, which is an action. Maybe doing a מצוה comes before reading, so the rule does not prove רב's order.

keyTerms.meaning: Did you hear him say this?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is rejecting רבי יהושע בן קרחה's rule. It agrees with his rule, and is only asking whether that rule reaches far enough to cover תפילין.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דַּאֲמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה —
phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said
to put one reading before another reading,
phrases.notes: He means the שמע paragraph before the והיה אם שמוע paragraph. Both are things you read.

phrases.english: but reading before doing, did you hear him say that?!
phrases.notes: The "doing" here is putting on תפילין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דַּאֲמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 25 by limiting רבי יהושע בן קרחה's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using רבי יהושע בן קרחה to support רב's order
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His rule only orders one reading against another reading. It says nothing about a reading against an action like תפילין.

steps.title: A story shows רב put on תפילין before reading שמע
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: רב חייא בר אשי saw רב put on תפילין first and read שמע afterward, so רב does not follow רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And besides that, does רב really hold like רבי יהושע בן קרחה? But רב חייא בר אשי said: Many times I stood before רב. First he washed his hands, made a ברכה, taught us our lesson, put on תפילין, and only then read קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second attack on the answer from step 25 (that רב follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה). A story shows רב doing the opposite order: תפילין first, then שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 claimed רב puts accepting עול מלכות שמים (reading שמע) before עול מצות (putting on תפילין). But this eyewitness story shows רב put on תפילין and only then read שמע. So the answer cannot be right about רב.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; a second challenge is coming
He taught us our lesson (our chapter)

phrases.english: And furthermore, does he really hold
phrases.notes: "He" is רב. The גמרא is adding a second problem on top of the one in step 26.

phrases.english: like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha?
But didn't Rav Chiyya bar Ashi say:
Many times I was standing
before Rav,
and he would first wash his hands,
and make a blessing, and teach us our lesson,
and put on tefillin,
and then read the Shema.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, מִי סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה? וְהָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent challenge to the answer of step 25, alongside step 26's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה and puts שמע before תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An eyewitness report shows רב regularly put on תפילין before reading שמע, the opposite order.

steps.title: Blocking the escape that it was too early for שמע
steps.stepSummary: One might say רב put on תפילין first only because it was not yet time for שמע. The גמרא answers: then the story would be pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it was before the time for קריאת שמע had arrived, then what is the point of רב חייא בר אשי's testimony?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way out of step 27 and then rejects it. If it was simply too early for שמע, the order would be obvious and there would be no reason to report it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The possible defense: רב put on תפילין first only because שמע could not be read yet. The rejection: a careful eyewitness report must be teaching something, and "he waited for the right time" teaches nothing. This leaves step 27's challenge standing for now.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; brings in a possible answer

phrases.english: And if you will say:
it was when the time for reading Shema had not yet come,
if so, what is the point of the testimony
of Rav Chiyya bar Ashi?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: בִּדְלָא מְטָא זְמַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, אִם כֵּן מַאי אַסְהַדְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a defense against step 27 and immediately pushes it away.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the story happened before the time for שמע.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If that were so, the story would teach nothing, and a reported testimony must have a point.

steps.title: The story teaches that learning משנה needs a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The story does have a point: it shows that even learning משנה needs a ברכת התורה, against the view that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The story comes to reject the one who says you do not need a ברכה before learning משנה. It teaches us that even for משנה you must make a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 28's question. The testimony was not about the order of תפילין and שמע. It was about רב making a ברכה before teaching משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 asked what the story teaches if it was simply too early for שמע. The answer: its lesson is that רב said a ברכה before teaching his lesson, which proves משנה needs a ברכת התורה too. So the story can describe a time before שמע was due, and it says nothing against רב following רבי יהושע בן קרחה.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude (reject) the one who says

phrases.english: It comes to exclude the one who says
that for Mishnah one does not need to make a blessing,
it teaches us
that even for Mishnah one must also make a blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִמַּאן דְּאָמַר לַמִּשְׁנָה אֵין צָרִיךְ לְבָרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28's question by showing what the story really teaches, which also defuses step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the purpose of a source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story was told to show the order רב used for תפילין and שמע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story was told to show that רב made a ברכת התורה before teaching משנה. The order was only because שמע's time had not yet come.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a practical rule: learning משנה also requires ברכת התורה.

steps.title: Still, רב's order remains a problem
steps.stepSummary: Even after all this, רב's practice of reading שמע before putting on תפילין is still hard to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, it is a difficulty for רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main problem. Step 26 showed that רבי יהושע בן קרחה does not explain רב's order, so רב reading שמע before תפילין still clashes with the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 only removed the second challenge (step 27). The first challenge (step 26) still stands: רבי יהושע בן קרחה spoke only about the order of the paragraphs. So רב reading שמע before putting on תפילין still needs an explanation, and the next step gives one.

phrases.english: In any case, it is a difficulty for Rav!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם קַשְׁיָא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the open difficulty from steps 24 and 26 after settling the side issue in steps 27-29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's practice of reading שמע before putting on תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא puts תפילין before שמע, and the רבי יהושע בן קרחה explanation failed in step 26, so רב's behavior is still unexplained.

steps.title: The messenger was late with the תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב's order was not his choice: the messenger bringing his תפילין came late, so he read שמע on time without them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was the messenger who messed up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem simply. רב did not plan to read שמע before תפילין. His תפילין arrived late, and he did not want to miss the time for שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer turns רב's behavior from a rule into a one-time accident. רב agrees with the ברייתא that תפילין come first. That day he simply had no תפילין in time.
steps.whatToRemember: רב really agrees that תפילין should come before שמע. The one time he read שמע first was because his תפילין came late.

phrases.english: It was the messenger who messed up.
phrases.notes: He means the person who was supposed to bring רב his תפילין was late.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלוּחָא הוּא דְּעַוֵּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 30's difficulty and closes the discussion about רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the case as an unusual circumstance
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב held as a rule that שמע comes before תפילין.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב followed the ברייתא's order. His תפילין were delayed, so he read שמע on time without them.

steps.title: Reading שמע without תפילין is like false testimony
steps.stepSummary: עולא says that reading שמע without תפילין is like giving false testimony about yourself.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Anyone who reads קריאת שמע without תפילין is as if he gave false testimony about himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a new teaching about how serious it is to read שמע without wearing תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual explanation is that in שמע a person says he ties the תפילין on his arm and head. If he is not wearing them, his own words testify to something untrue.

phrases.english: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע בְּלֹא תְּפִילִּין,
phrases.english: Anyone who reads the Shema without tefillin,
it is as if he gives false testimony about himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: כָּל הַקּוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע בְּלֹא תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case of רב to a general statement about reading שמע without תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading שמע without תפילין is like testifying falsely about oneself.

steps.title: Like a קרבן missing its partner offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן compares reading שמע without תפילין to bringing a קרבן without the offering that goes with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is as if he brought an עולה without a מנחה, or a זבח without נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: A second statement on the same subject, using a different picture. רבי יוחנן compares it to a קרבן that is missing its partner offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה normally comes with a מנחה, and a זבח with wine נסכים. The main offering still counts, but it is incomplete. In the same way, שמע without תפילין counts, but it is missing a piece. This is softer than עולא's "false testimony" picture.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח
A flour offering that comes along with the עולה
An animal offering, such as a שלמים
Wine libations poured with an offering

steps.whatToRemember: Both עולא and רבי יוחנן teach that שמע should be read while wearing תפילין. עולא calls it false testimony. רבי יוחנן calls it an incomplete offering.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
It is as if he offered a burnt-offering without a meal-offering,
and a sacrifice without libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּאִילּוּ הִקְרִיב עוֹלָה בְּלֹא מִנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, parallel statement on the same topic as עולא in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמע without תפילין is like a קרבן missing the offering that goes with it: it counts, but it is incomplete.

steps.title: How to accept the complete yoke of Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן begins a new teaching about someone who wants to accept עול מלכות שמים completely. Only the opening is here; the instructions come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן also said: A person who wants to take upon himself the full, complete yoke of the kingdom of Heaven...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from רבי יוחנן, and here it only states the setup: "someone who wants to accept עול מלכות שמים completely." This line prepares the next move, which will tell us what that person should do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 33 used a sharp negative comparison: שמע without תפילין is like a קרבן missing its offering. This new statement turns that around into a positive goal, a שלמה, complete, acceptance of עול מלכות שמים. The word שלמה hints that there is an incomplete way and a complete way, and the full recipe is about to be given.

keyTerms.meaning: The yoke of the kingdom of Heaven: accepting הקב"ה as King, which is done mainly through קריאת שמע
Complete, full; not missing any part
One who wants or seeks to do something
That he should take upon himself, accept

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a full statement yet. The sentence stops in the middle, and רבי יוחנן's actual instructions come right after it. Don't look for the answer in this line.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
One who wants to accept upon himself
the complete yoke of the kingdom of Heaven

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם שְׁלֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two statements criticizing קריאת שמע without תפילין, רבי יוחנן now starts a positive teaching about the complete way to accept עול מלכות שמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: the statement is about a person who wants to accept עול מלכות שמים fully. The practical instructions follow in the continuation.
